content: Journeyman haberdasher in St Bride's parish near the Fleet
Brings Stratford word from the Bell in Carter Lane
He will carry the letter and he will not invent the answer. The last question is the one he makes you hear.
On Tuesday he read the shop-ticket twice, called the three debts near five pound, and did not ask you to pay.
He will carry a letter three days unopened, and he will ask about the porch.
From St Bride's, and back since Saturday. The shop keeps him, so Thursday's fetch is yours. He had forgot the twenty-sixth until the almanac.
He will carry three versions of a fire and stop the sentence before God keep you.
He can hold three weeks of London in one meeting, and he will name Sadler without offering to carry the debt.
With his master's ledger open, he affects not to know a player, including his brother.
He brings a father's sentence whole, eats the half you cannot chew, and keeps the rind.
